cells.tense: Here, with the pen, the growth is happening without being forced.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Keep caring for what you already tend, and set down the picture of how it should turn out — do the work without holding the ending.
cells.core:
The care is working, and it is not working by strain. Something you tend is coming along at the speed it needs, and your part in it — the conditions, the attention, the waiting — has been enough. You can tell because none of it feels like pushing. Tending this way leaves you with energy afterward, which is how you know nothing is being forced. The patience is the point, not the price.

What keeps this going is leaving the result unfinished. The thing you are helping is still coming into shape, and holding it loosely is what lets it get there. Put down the version you keep picturing in advance. Keep the care and let what it becomes arrive when it arrives. That is the whole move, and it is enough.

cells.tense: A future that cannot be written in is already being rehearsed in the mind.
cells.act: sketch the whole of it badly, on one page, and keep the sketch
cells.ask: When you catch yourself writing the ending ahead of time, sketch it on one page instead, badly, then set it aside and stay with what is here.
cells.core:
Checked in on too often, the thing you care for has less room to grow. The care is genuine, but it has started reaching ahead — writing the outcome before it exists, watching for signs, solving problems that have not arrived. Some of the attention meant to help has turned into steering. Run that way, the person you care for feels watched instead of held, and you carry a future you cannot control.

What brings this back is dreaming from what has already happened rather than what might. Take what you have lived and let it guide your next step — nothing past it. Sketch the shape roughly, keep the sketch, put it away. The way ahead opens a step at a time. Stand where you are and let what is coming come without you managing it.
cells.sheetLine: The care has reached past today into a future you cannot write.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
cells.act: remember what drew you and face it again
cells.ask: Think back to what once drew you toward making something, and turn toward that again — no plan, no progress, just face it once more.
cells.core:
The ground where things grew from you has gone quiet. You keep the motion of caring without the pull toward anything in particular — going through the moves, nothing reaching toward light. From outside it reads as steady, as someone who does not need much, as fine alone. Inside, nothing is unfolding.

What was there before the quiet is worth going back to. There was something you once wanted to make or grow, before it got practical, before it got shelved. Go back and face that again — not to produce anything, just to remember what it was like to be pulled. Wanting something is not a debt you owe. The pull returns by being turned toward, not by being summoned harder.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you are already writing in, holding what you did not choose.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Something you carry for someone was not yours to pick up — set it down on purpose and let your hands stay empty for a while.
cells.core:
There is a role in this room you have been filling without having picked it up. Other people experience you as the one who keeps things going, and the effort sits on you now — the depletion is real. But the role has not been claimed. It runs as background, as something to get through rather than something you are doing. That gap between what you give and what you notice giving is what wears you down.

Setting something down is not abandoning the person you help. It is laying aside one thing that is no longer yours to carry. Choose what you did not sign up for, and put it down for a stretch. Let your hands stay empty. Care returns to a person who has their own hands free.
cells.sheetLine: You carry a role you did not choose and can set down.

attempts.check: One unsupported thing: the Unacknowledged cell risks assuming the care has gone on a long time and is imposed, not freely chosen — the record only says the role is unchosen and the person feels depleted. The reader could say the care was taken on, not put on them, or that they knew all along. The ask survives that: the pause in one moment belongs to whoever is holding one thing they never wanted to hold. The sentence that serves the writer more than them is 'You do see it as yours' in the disowned core; the pause must not smuggle an accusation about how the role arrived.
